notes.title: A report from the testing branch, and a teaser [CHANGELOG]
notes.notes:
Hello hunters,

we’d like to thank you for all the feedback and testing you’re doing on the experimental branch, it really means a lot and helps us make the game the best it can be.

On that note, we have some more good news for you today. Our devs, hard at work in the code mines, are here to deliver some new changes. Meaning, we’re updating the experimental branch with a bunch of rebalances and bug fixes. You can find the changelog for that below.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/2dEi78T.png[/img]

We know you hunters, and we know you well. You're aching to get back into the hunt. You can practically smell the prey. Well, now you can also see it. We're giving you a teaser of our new enemy, the terrifying Elder Vampire. Here's what our devs had to say about this one:

[i]Most beasts are dangerous because of their enormous strength, not their intelligence. What if a monster had the strength of a beast and the intelligence of a man? Elder Vampires are foes to be afraid of. They are capable of dealing high physical damage as well as weakening hunters with their rituals.[/i]

Note, that this enemy is already available on the experimental branch, this is just a teaser for the folks waiting for the full update on the main branch.

[b]Experimental Branch Changelog:[/b]
[list]
[*] Re-balance of corruption on cursed weapons. The corruption will grow quicker when using cursed weapons and items.
[*] Lowered the amount of food that can be acquired through scavenging.
[*] Fixed missing icon on Greatswords' "Counterstrike" abilities.
[*] Fixed missing rewards from the "Dark Influence" research.
[*] Added higher costs of all research projects.
[*] Added information about hunter's max level.
[/list]

These are not all the changes that are coming, as we are still waiting for the full report from the QA. We're hard at work so expect more updates soon!

Alright, that's it from us, once again thank you all for posting your feedback and bug reports, we really appreciate them. If you have any questions, concerns, or nice words for our team, please leave a comment!

Thank you, and hope you'll enjoy these new changes
Your Shockworks

notes.title: Update 2.0 on test now! [CHANGELOG]
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/ZiZXRBy.png[/img]

Hey Hunters,

We know you've been waiting a long time for this, but we finally have an update we promised you a long time ago, to hit the PC!

First, it lands on the [i]experimental[/i] branch so that you can test it in a safe environment, as it brings so many new changes. We will organize a separate QA session with our publisher around the same time to ensure that the update is worth the wait. Below this post, you can find a MASSIVE changelog detailing all of the changes the update brings.

We cordially invite you to check out the new update and share your experience, as we deeply appreciate all your feedback. 

Now, for a bit of an explanation, because you deserve it. This Alder’s Blood update has been in the works for a while and has remained our priority all throughout the process. We gained a lot of feedback from the community and we knew how to fix the game. But the thing is that Alder’s Blood is a complicated game with many systems overlapping each other. A simple change in one place has a huge impact in a different spot, which had to be adjusted as well. In the end, we had to change or at least re-set up pretty much any system in the game, and that takes time.

We promise to focus more on frequent communication with you here on the Steam forums. However, the fact we were inexperienced during the development of Alder’s Blood made this title almost impossible to enhance with bigger content updates, but we’ll try to regularly patch it and maybe add something little from time to time.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/oWyLpHm.png[/img]

It’s a different game now, and we really do hope you will enjoy it more. Let’s take a look at what has changed:

[h1][b]Highlights:[/b][/h1]

[b]Corruption system:[/b]
The most controversial feature of Alder’s Blood has been completely reworked. No longer will your hunters suffer the corruption effects just because they fight monsters, or take part in missions. The original idea treated hunters as expendables, but it didn’t work out well.
Now hunters gain corruption only from the listed sources:
[list][*]using weapons or items with “Cursed item” trait,
[*]banishing monsters,
[*]some random events.[/list]
Now you control your corruption gain. Cursed items are more powerful, so you can choose between a powerful but costly approach, and a moderate yet safer one.
So, our previous design of expandable hunters is now optional, you decide whether you want to keep your hunters safe, exploit then discard them or something in-between.

[b]Wind system:[/b]
In the release version the wind was too random, so we stopped it from changing its direction until we could fix it. Now the wind will show you the direction it's going to change to, a turn before. So that you can prepare, and hide in the right place.

[b]Darkness system:[/b]
The Darkness system was planned as a big thing that brings variety to the game. From looking at your comments, all it brought was frustration. We are turning off the system completely for the time being.

[b]Ranged weapons:[/b]
You will notice that Ranged weapons cannot be used in melee. Only shotguns break this rule. Keep your riflemen safe!

[b]Attack of opportunity:[/b]
Ranged weapons cannot be used in melee, so why not just move away? Well, because your hunter will get hit by the monster when disengaging. Be careful when you commit to melee, or where you move, cause that attack of opportunity may hurt!

[b]New weapons:[/b]
We’ve added 23 new weapons to deal some damage to the enemies. We think that everybody should find something interesting to arm their hunters with. Weapons availability also changed. Many of them can be purchased in shops from the start of the game, as long as you have the cash.

[b]Critical Damage:[/b]
Every weapon has a new statistic now: Critical Hit Chance. Critical hit deals 125% base damage.

[b]New abilities effects:[/b]
Some of the new gear features new abilities’ effects. The big highlight in these sections are push and pull effects. Remember the attack of opportunity feature? Pushing or pulling enemies away from your hunters is one of the ways to deal with that.
We also added a smoke bomb that can create a temporary cloud of smoke that can hide your hunters like bushes or tall grass.

[b]New enemies:[/b]
We’ve added 3 new enemy types to the game:
[b][i]Bat swarm:[/i][/b]
A low-level enemy with knockdown resistance, and short, but 360 vision range. Look out for it’s Bleeding attack! A simple addition to add more variety.
[b][i]Woods Witch:[/i][/b]
This enemy is capable of buffing her fellow monsters with new Status effects:
[list][*][b]Armored[/b]: armored enemy receives only 50% damage.
[*][b]Wrath[/b]: enemy with wrath will deal extra 25% damage.[/list]
Ah, and she can also heal other enemies. It would be wise to prioritise her in your battles.
[b][i]Elder Vampire:[/i][/b]
Mini-boss type of enemy. They can deal some serious damage from afar and close by. You can encounter them in the new Blackwells side questline.

[b]Research wagon:[/b]
Progression was tightly packed with your main quest. Now we open this up with availability of weapons in stores, but also with a Research wagon. Research takes time, but can unlock new gear and weapons at your own pace.

[b]Hunters roster and levels:[/b]
Hunters now have their max level capped at 6. You need to carefully choose what Traits you want them to have, as they can only have a few!
Also, your caravan has a limit to the amount of hunters that can travel with you at the same time. This amount can be increased through the aforementioned Research wagon.

[b]New traits:[/b]
We’ve added a couple of new Traits to the game, including:
Weapon Mastery Trait giving a hunter a 25% damage bonus when using weapons of a specific class.
Dark One gives a hunter an extra 25% damage dealt when using cursed weapons.
Cursed Item trait indicates a cursed item (what a twist!), they are generally more powerful but they corrupt hunters who use them.
We’ve also added traits that are unlocked through the Research wagon and affect the whole caravan.

[b]Factions Contracts:[/b]
These smaller missions can provide you with some needed XP, as well as faction loyalty that can get you some unique gear. Previously, it was tied to the side missions, now you can get loyalty points through contracts. Each faction has 3 levels of contracts, adding 12 new missions with different levels of complexity.

[b]New questline:[/b]
House Blackwell gained a new quest line featuring a new Elder Vampire enemy. It unlocks after the destruction of the Tower of Love in the main quest.

This concludes the list of major changes to the game in this update. We really hope you will enjoy them, and give us your thoughts and feedback. This beta version of the update will stay on the experimental branch for a week or two, until we finish gathering feedback from both you and our QA team. Once all is set and done, we will move the update to the main branch.

Thank you for your patience Hunters, and see you on the hunt!

notes.title: What's coming with the BIG update?
notes.notes:
Hey Hunters!

After a whole bunch of patches and updates - we are back! Thanks to your feedback, we are able to improve Alder's Blood everyday. 

I know you're waiting for something big, that's why we've decided to share more information and details about 1.1.0 or "On the road update"

We've decided to put all 3 of the last Kickstarter stretch goals into this, one, big update. Mostly because we had our worries about balance if they would be brought into chunks. Below, we have a list of new features and changes you'll see in this update. Some are already done, some are in progress, while others are still waiting to be finished. Ok, so let's go:

[list]
[*]Research wagon in the camp: This will allow you to unlock new weapons and gear at your own pace, and tied everything to the mission progression.
[*]"Global traits": part of the research wagon update, they will grant bonuses similar to hunters' traits, but they are not tied to a specific hunter.
[*]More optional missions: these focus on building loyalty with the factions.
[*]New enemy, "Licker": vampiric type, enemy, with an ability to stun hunters with ultrasound. This one is close to being finished.
[/list]

[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/030/654/523/632b4fd83af0e719d9b85fe310304791_original.gif?ixlib=rb-2.1.0&w=700&fit=max&v=1600438891&auto=format&gif-q=50&q=92&s=2105f8345bb6a2b29017811198969477[/img]

[list]
[*]New enemy, "Whisperer": this one comes in a package with some new status effects, like Armored, Wrath, and Shielded.
[*]Corruption system revamp: Corruption proved to be a controversial concept for the community, and since release, we were looking for ways to make it better. Fortunately, it needed more design work, than coding, and this update is a good time to introduce the changes. It requires a lot of rebalancing of weapons and, items, especially magic-oriented. In this iteration, hunters will be corrupted by making mistakes (getting exposed, getting hit by enemies), or by using corrupted items (cursed items and magic). These changes will also allow for a more aggressive playstyle without the need to sacrifice the hunters all the time.
[*]Overwatch abilities: these will be both melee and ranged so that you can make ambushes even more fun. With the changes to the corruption system, the overwatch will have its place now.
[*]"Push" and "Pull" abilities: want to pull en enemy into the trap? Or maybe kick him into overwatch ability of another hunter? That's what these abilities are for.
[*]Smokescreens: a simple grenade that will spawn a terrain similar to grass that hunters can hide in.
[/list]

[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/030/654/553/ce3bac3e70f851c0c65dd5d9c488af63_original.png?ixlib=rb-2.1.0&w=700&fit=max&v=1600439027&auto=format&frame=1&lossless=true&s=9b1a07d6aacccad2dc1cf146346e68b1[/img]

There are some other, smaller changes planned, mostly UX based. We don't have a release date for this update yet, as we want to be sure, it's a good, enjoyable one. We will keep you posted on the development process. Stay tuned! :)

In the meantime, please consider wishlisting There is No Light, the project seems really promising! It's a post-apocalyptic pixel-art action-adventure set in a grim underground world. We recently came across the game on Kickstarter and immediately fell in love!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1132980/There_Is_No_Light/

Your Shockworks

notes.title: Today's update
notes.notes:
Hello hunters! 

First of all, we wanted to thank you all for the feedback that you provided us since the launch day. We tried to reply to every comment, but if we didn’t, be aware that we read every post.

We prepared a patch 1.0.5 that addresses most of the issues you found in the game. We fixed bugs and rebalanced the Corruption system (full patch notes are at the end of this post). This is definitely not the last update we will bring to Alder’s Blood, so keep the feedback flowing, we really want it!

[h1]Testing environment 
[/h1]

To ensure the quality of the new updates we created a special testing environment for it. We created a special branch on Steam called “experimental”, where the new build will be uploaded. This branch is available to everybody and instructions on how to access it are listed below.

DISCLAIMER: We cannot guarantee saves compatibility between the two of the branches. The main branch saves should work on experimental just fine, but not the other way around.

[h2]How to access the experimental branch?
[/h2]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/mXs0Dgu.png[/img]

First, you need to right-click on Alder’s Blood in your library. Choose preferences and then “Betas” bookmark. From a dropdown menu choose “experimental” and wow, you just have access to the new branch.

When you would like to come back to the main branch, choose NONE - Opt-out of all beta programs.

[h2]Why we did it this way?
[/h2]
Since we are a small team of 6 people there is still a possibility that this update will not be perfect. We want to give it a spin for a few days in this testing environment and tinker a bit in various values, see your feedback and react with changes.

[h2]What next?
[/h2]
We will keep the update on the experimental branch for a couple of days and when we decide it’s ready, we will push it to the main branch. 
We will keep this branch operating and use it to test some other ideas for balance, new weapons, items, and features. With your feedback, we believe we can make this game better.

After patch 1.0.5, we will introduce the first content update. It will feature a new hunter skin, more avatars and color variations for already existing skins. We will also add more random missions, so you can have more to do in between main and side quests.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jibXVNE.png[/img]

[b]Changes[/b]:
[list]
[*] Changed the way corruption is applied to hunters. Now only hostile hunter actions will build-up corruption. Corruption values on weapons have been readjusted, and the negative traits threshold has been increased.
[*] Changed Hangman’s Finger Charm to decrease the corruption build-up on a hunter who equips it. Multiple charms of this kind can be equipped to increase the effect.
[*] Small changes in damage values/stamina costs on Double-barreled Shotgun and Marksman Rifle. 
[*] Added a button to the options menu on missions to open the Codex.
[*] Added “E” keyboard shortcut for weapon swapping.
[*] Updated City’s Outskirts graphics.
[*] Re-enabled ironman mode.
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed broken cinematics during some of the missions.
[*] Fixed an issue, where taking a freshly recruited hunter on a mission cause various issues.
[*] Fixed “Critical Damage” sound not taking sound settings into consideration.
[*] Fixed weather widget tooltip not showing up.
[*] Fixed an issue, where a monster walking through multiple traps would freeze the game.
[*] Fixed “Kill all monsters” objective counting non-killable enemies.
[*] Fixed sleeping enemies getting awake on save load.
[*] Fixed conversation voices not being affected by the Voices sound volume slider.
[*] Fixed an issue with stat-based Steam achievements.
[*] Fixed a couple of missing and wrong translations.
[*] Fixed strategy voices and weak damage indicator not respecting game volume settings.
[*] Fixed mission restarting killing hunters in the next loaded save.
[*] Fixed autosave using only the last save slot.
[*] Fixed darkness morphing any enemy (even those essential to an objective).
[*] Fixed older saves missing on new events.
[*] Fixed resisted damage text being too small.
[*] Fixed Deathwalker status indicator.
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/sruaOMk.png[/img]

[list]
[*] Random events are temporarily disabled.
[/list]

Thank you and stay safe!
Your Shockworks

notes.title: DevLog: How NOT to play Alder's Blood
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/P29nZ9G.png[/img]

Hey everybody! Here are some gameplay tips from Michał how (not) to play Alder’s Blood. If you follow our social media posts and streams, you could already see some tips on how to deal with the monsters. Today we are going to focus on clumsy actions that can easily and quickly kill your hunters.

[b]Running blindly into the fray
[/b]Alder’s Blood is primarily a stealth game and any hasty action usually ends up a disaster. Movement system in AB is flexible, so you don’t have to worry about ending your turn too early. Move around slowly, scan the area with you hunter sense and position your hunter accordingly. The worst thing that can happen is to walk onto a Shrieker that will alarm a Stalker and a Floater. With the added Reaction System your hunter will either die instantly or will be locked in place awaiting his death in the enemy’s turn.

[previewyoutube=tkyFJWF38ms;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Attacking head-on
[/b]We mentioned that Reaction System, right? When monsters spot a hunter, they will immediately use a reaction of their own. And with big guys like a Brawler, this can be very, very painful. Distracting a monster wth a pebble and then attacking from the rear is the way to go in most cases.

[previewyoutube=lGYQRBXUE2I;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Using most of your Stamina and not ending a fight
[/b]Every attack or use of an item costs Stamina and when a hunter runs out of Stamina he looses a whole next turn. Keeping that in mind, it’s not really a good idea to span attacks that won’t kill a high threat target. Your hunter has only 1 stamina bar left and the monster is still standing? Get ready to get knocked down in enemy turn. With one monster only it may not be that big of a deal, but if the group is bigger, or some new monsters join the party, you will be left with only two hunters at your disposal.

[previewyoutube=myzrvFOzIDA;full][/previewyoutube]

That’s all for today folks. We hope you will find those tips useful when the release of Alder’s Blood hits! TTYS! 

Your Shockworks

notes.title: Alder's Blood DevLog - Monsters' Reactions
notes.notes:
Hey guys, Shockworks here with a report of probably the biggest update to Alder’s Blood yet!

Since we are done with the “guts” of the game we can finally slow down and look at the details of Alder’s Blood, talk with the community about their experience and polish the game.

One of the aspects that we felt was something still needing changes was monsters AI. If you played for at least a few hours, you could quickly find a way to abuse the system and instead of playing a stealth game you would play a hit and run game.

I’m not gonna lie, that we were really scared to change that so far into the development of the game, but we took the risk...and it was totally worth it!

[previewyoutube=-2nRV2SdAm4;full][/previewyoutube]

The question remains: how does it work now?
When a hunter walks into the vision cone of an enemy he will immediately stop now and the monster reactions start.
This can be a free attack for the monster or an alarming scream, it depends on which monster spotted the hunter.

But wait, there’s more! 
Remember how pebbles work? Hunter can throw them to change the direction of the monster, god for cleaning up movement lines right? Well, now every sound will trigger the same reaction.

[previewyoutube=NnMBjjqRZIA;full][/previewyoutube]

In practice, you will have to be way more careful with any firearm within the game. As it can be as deadly to the monster as to your hunter.

These two things changed the way you play Alder’s Blood quite dramatically, but only for the better. You need to be more careful with what you do, use your gear way more and try to look for creative ways of dealing with dangerous situations.

[previewyoutube=53lB-XR-otM;full][/previewyoutube]

Want an example? Here you go!

Here we have a Brawler, quite a strong enemy, more than capable of trashing a single hunter all on his own. We know we won’t be able to bring him down with one shot of the rifle and by shooting we will trigger a reaction. But we have some traps equipped, so let’s use them.
First, let’s place the traps between our gunner and the monster and then open fire. The Brawler takes some damage, then tries to attack the hunter and walks right into the trap!

[previewyoutube=9P7315pMvFE;full][/previewyoutube]

We are really happy with how the system evolved and we hope you will like it as well. If you are a Backer with the Beta access, you will have the chance to test it very very soon.

If you want to help us and make Alder’s Blood a successful game, wishlist it on Steam!

Thank you,

notes.title: DevLog: Corruption
notes.notes:
No, it’s not going to be about politics, but… a character progression in Alder’s Blood! ;)

Yup, we have this thing called Corruption in our game and we didn’t think we should talk too much about it, but it’s a pretty big mechanic in the game, so I think it deserves its own DevLog.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/LZGJxmp.jpg[/img]

If you followed us for some time you probably know that it’s the decaying corpse of God that is responsible for all the troubles in the grim world of Alder’s Blood. Our hunters are the only ones capable of getting rid of this problem as they are the closest creatures to their deceased Father...but it’s also their weakness.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/xBCxGUK.jpg[/img]

Since they are so close to their god, they are also more vulnerable to its corrupting power. With time it wearies down a hunter, or can even drive him mad as the beasts he once hunted.

How does it translate to gameplay? Hunters gather corruption points as they:
[list]
[*] take part in missions,
[*] attack monsters directly (poison or bleeding doesn’t count!),
[*] take damage from monsters,
[*] use magic or corrupted weapons and items.
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/mLLXU96.jpg[/img]

When a threshold is breaching during a mission a hunter will gain a negative trait. This may result in decreased maximum health or stamina, or worse performance in camping tasks.

The corruption grows in hunters with time, quicker in more aggressive hunters. How can you counter it? You can’t. Once the corruption level is too high, the hunter can go mad and attack its own crew. Not only you will lose that hunter, but others may get hurt.  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/a5nmzK5.jpg[/img]

The only real option for you is to use a sacrifice ritual. Hunters know that they are not invincible, so they can choose to forfeit their lives to strengthen the younger generation. A more leveled up hunter is also a hunter with higher corruption, by using the sacrifice mechanic a portion of experience can be transferred to a recruit to start fresh.
The trick is to know when the time comes to leave the hunting grounds.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/LE2EqKF.jpg[/img]

This is quite a gloomy mechanic, but also a one that should prevent players from losing too much progress with the death of the more elite fighters. We hope you will like this idea.

That’s all for today and see you in the next one!

notes.title: The Alder's Blood demo feels like Bloodborne's sneaky turn-based cousin
notes.notes:
Hunting werewolves is dangerous business in Alder's Blood. For starters, they're flupping enormous fangorious man-dogs, which is bad enough. Second, they've got a great sense of smell, which isn't so great when your cadre of monster hunters (who look like they've just walked straight out of Bloodborne) haven't bathed in weeks. Stealth is order of the day here, giving this squad tactics game a very different feel from its peers.

Developed by Polish studio Shockwork Games, Alder's Blood has been in the works for a long time now. It's pretty far along in development and due out in the first quarter of 2020, but the developers are raising some extra funds to push it over the finish line in style. Their new Kickstarter is fully funded already (to the humble tune of $12,000), and now they've released a playable demo so that you can try it for yourself and decide whether you want to throw a few dollars at it.

There's some rough edges to the demo. There's the occasional bit of placeholder text, and the script hasn't been fully localised so expect some grammatical fumbles as English isn't the studio's native tongue. Beyond that, it's a nice three-mission-long peek at the game's interlocking systems, and great showcase for its dark comic-book style art, which reminds me a bit of Darkest Dungeon. A fair comparison, given how fragile your squad can feel when best laid plans fail.

In turn-based combat, you'll be hopping your hunters between patches of long grass, making sure they're downwind of anything with a good nose, and weighing up whether you want to use risky swords, noisy guns or exhausting ritual magic (fuelled by a vaguely Souls-esque stamina meter) to dispatch the prowling beasties. Between fights, you'll manage your nomadic hunter team and decide who's gathering food, resting or standing watch at camp each night.

You can download the demo on the Alder's Blood Kickstarter page. Grab it quick, as Shockwork say it'll only be available for "a limited period of time". The full game is due out early next year on Steam and GOG.

notes.title: Alder's Blood looks like a turn-based tactical Bloodborne
notes.notes:
Alder’s Blood seems like a turn-based tactics game precision-made to fit my interests. A little bit XCOM, a little bit Darkest Dungeon and a whole lot of Bloodborne. It’s due out this year, and last night developers Shockwork Games released a new trailer, showing off a world that they call a “fusion of dark Victorian fantasy and wild west”. That means flintlock rifles and blades at dusk, as long-coated and masked Hunters sneak around, chopping up werewolves, vampires and more otherworldly and ‘orrible servants of an undead god. See the grim darkness below.
